references.text: The preceding context where the first and second brother take the woman as wife and die childless ([ref:Luk 20:29-30|Luke 20:29-30]). The verse continues the same account with the third and the remaining seven brothers.
The law of levirate marriage in [ref:5 Mos 25:5-6|Deut 25:5-6] is the background for this entire account, where the brothers in turn take the deceased's wife to raise up offspring for him.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:20-22|Mark 12:20-22] tells the same story of the seven brothers who all took the woman as wife, left no children, and died.
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:25-27|Matt 22:25-27] recounts the same account of the seven brothers who married the woman and died without leaving any children.
